# omx-dsp / fuzz_laws

omx-dsp's own fuzz target `fuzz_laws` ([source](source/fuzz_laws.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over omx-dsp 0.27.0 (FreeMixer/omx-dsp at a0ee1dfe).

Reads up to 64 calls, each picked by a selector byte. Its arguments are raw float words where a law takes any value, two-byte values mapped onto a law's travel, selector bytes (block lengths, pan leg, rate) and single bits (mutes). The calls cover the clamps and unit knob, dB to linear and back in both forms, the pan and balance laws, the fader coefficient, the linear ramp, the wet/dry mix and cross-fade, and the one-pole constructors, rescale and step. Each result is checked against its law, and the contract ledger is read after each call.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against libomxdsp.a, which build.sh compiles from omx-dsp's five src/*.c files with -DOMX_CONTRACTS and -ffp-contract=off; the laws are inline in the headers. The Makefile's own fuzz build uses native clang with libFuzzer, which this build replaces with the standard driver.
- omx-contract's headers are pinned to the tag v3.4.0 (1169c701), where the library's Makefile uses whichever omx-contract is installed, at or above its packaging floor of 3.1.0.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- omx_clampf, omx_clamp_or and omx_unit land inside their travel for any word. A word already inside comes back unchanged, and a non-finite word given to omx_clamp_or reads as the declared default ([lines 61-103](source/fuzz_laws.c#L61-L103)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- dB to linear is never negative and, inside +-150 dB, finite and positive, in both the libm and polynomial forms. Linear to dB keeps its floor and stays finite for any finite word; the polynomial form stays finite ([lines 109-162](source/fuzz_laws.c#L109-L162)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Inside +-150 dB, converting dB to linear and back gives the original dB to within 0.01 dB ([lines 125-132](source/fuzz_laws.c#L125-L132)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The pan law is constant power: the squares of the two legs add up to 1 (to 1e-5) on [-1, 1] ([lines 168-174](source/fuzz_laws.c#L168-L174)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The balance law never boosts: both legs are in [0, 1] and one of them is 1, at any pan word. The fader coefficient is finite and not negative, and 0 when the strip or the DCA is muted, for a fader level on a 16-bit grid of [-200, 60] dB and send and DCA gains capped at 1e6 ([lines 178-211](source/fuzz_laws.c#L178-L211)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A ramp starts at the applied value (0 when that is not finite), never leaves the span of its two ends, and ends on its target ([lines 226-250](source/fuzz_laws.c#L226-L250)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- For samples on a 16-bit grid of [-8, 8], the wet/dry mix lies between the dry and wet samples, to 1e-5. For bodies on a 16-bit grid of [-4, 4], each cross-fade sample lies between the outgoing and incoming bodies, to 1e-5 ([lines 260-281](source/fuzz_laws.c#L260-L281)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The time and corner constructors give a pole in [0, 1) for any finite argument, and a rescaled pole stays in [0, 1]. For a state and an input on a 16-bit grid of [-4, 4], one filter step lies between the input and the state (to 1e-5), and the step returns the new state ([lines 288-320](source/fuzz_laws.c#L288-L320)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After each call, no contract of the library is recorded as broken, except the crossover token bands-partition-unity, which this harness never reaches ([lines 160-168](source/fuzz.h#L160-L168)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

| `asan_ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 2 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; ASan+UBSan never fires; memory refused only when forced | open |

Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch omx-dsp` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
